title: Quantum Therapeutics - Onprem Airgapped Discovery
summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood Private on-prem air-gapped deployment for regulated biotech workloads. Covered security controls (SOC2/ISO, KMS/HSM, SSO), offline update process, hardware topology (GPU counts, NVLink, PCIe fabric), network isolation, audit/export constraints, and pilot scope. AE + SE to send security pack, deployment checklist, and preliminary cost model. Agreed to run a short benchmark on-site and schedule follow-up with procurement and facilities.
topics: Hardware constraints: GPUs, NVLink, rack space
Security: KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Ethan from Redwood, I'm joined by Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Dr. Ana (CTO): Hi Ethan, doing well. Thanks for taking the time. We got the calendar notes, excited to dig in.
[00:12] Priya (SE): Hi Ana, hi team. Quick agenda: understand your regulatory constraints, current infra, what air-gapped means for you, then we can map Redwood Private capabilities and next steps.
[00:22] Samir (Head of IT): Sounds good. To be clear, Quantum Therapeutics handles PHI and IP; anything we run must be in our secure data center, no egress, no outbound to internet.
[00:32] Laura (Security): And we need auditable updates, attestation of binaries, support for HSM-backed keys for model encryption.
[00:40] Ethan: Totally understood. Can you walk me through your current stack for model serving and where you're seeing pain?
[00:47] Michael (ML Lead): Sure. Right now we have an internal inference cluster — a mix of A100s and older V100s — everything on our private fabric. We do model hosting in-house, but operationally it's costly. Latency is ok for research but not for production SLA. Also, model rollout and canarying are manual.
[01:05] Priya: Thanks, that matches many customers. For air-gapped, we have an on-prem package — control plane runs in your network, we can deliver signed artifacts and an offline installer. How often do you expect to update models and the runtime?
[01:16] Dr. Ana: For now, model updates are quarterly but security patches might be monthly. For our regulated pipelines, any model change must go through QA and validation.
[01:25] Samir: Also, facility constraints: our racks have limited PDU capacity; we have two bare-metal racks reserved, anything over 6kW per rack will be a problem. We can provision a private NVLink fabric but only up to 8 GPUs per host.
[01:38] Ethan: Ok. From a Redwood perspective, we support per-cluster configuration — you can pin model versions, define rollout policies (canary/A/B), and we provide tooling for offline updates. Our offline install uses signed tarballs, and we support operator-run update flows — you stage the package on an air-gapped USB / local repo, validate signatures with your HSM.
[01:55] Laura: How does the KMS/HSM integration work? We must ensure model keys never leave HSM; encryption at rest and in-use if possible.
[02:03] Priya: We integrate with on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11 for key wrapping. Models are stored encrypted; runtime fetches wrapped keys and unwraps within a secure enclave on the host. For customers that need it, we can work with an HSM attestation flow.
[02:18] Michael: Is there support for sealing the KV cache or is that ephemeral? We want to avoid any leakage between models.
[02:24] Priya: KV cache is process-local and ephemeral unless you opt into persistent cache. For multi-tenant hosts we run isolation containers and enforce strict FSGROUPs; for your use-case likely single-tenant hosts.
[02:35] Samir: Network topology — we won't allow outbound DNS. How does Redwood handle license checks or telemetry in an offline environment?
[02:42] Ethan: For fully air-gapped, telemetry is optional. License/seat activation can be done via a signed license file you upload. For licensing we support an offline handshake: you generate a CSR, we sign it, and you attest locally.
[02:55] Laura: Audit logs — we need tamper-evident logs and push to our SIEM. Can Redwood forward logs to our Splunk/ELK instance over the internal network?
[03:04] Priya: Yes, we can forward structured logs and traces to your SIEM over HTTPS/L4. For tamper-evidence we can include append-only hashes and optional write-once storage.
[03:14] Dr. Ana: Great. Any limits on model size or tokenizer support? Some of our models are custom 70B variants, and we may quantize.
[03:23] Priya: We support large models; runtime picks kernels and memory partitioning. For 70B you need enough GPU memory — typically 80GB-class or sharded across nodes with NVLink. We also support 4-bit and 8-bit quantization paths.
[03:36] Michael: For the 70B we tried sharded inference with no NVLink and latency was terrible. If we ensure NVLink interconnect, will Redwood take advantage of that topology?
[03:45] Priya: Yes, runtime can utilize NVLink for cross-GPU KV cache and attention broadcasts. We also provide recommended cluster topologies for low-SLO workloads.
[03:54] Samir: What about offline updates to the runtime itself? We can't just accept a random binary. We need a vetted upgrade process and rollback.
[04:02] Ethan: Understood. Our process for private deployments includes signed release artifacts, per-release release notes, and a rollback operator. We support staged rollouts: you can apply to a canary node in your lab, run your validation suite, then promote. We can also provide a pre-validation VM image to smoke-test.
[04:18] Laura: For compliance, will you provide SOC2 or ISO documentation? The vendor is expected to provide attestations even for private deployments.
[04:26] Ethan: Absolutely — we'll share SOC 2 Type II reports, data flow diagrams, and our internal secure development lifecycle docs. For private installs, we also provide a deployment security checklist to align with your auditors.
[04:38] Dr. Ana: Timeline — we're aiming to have a production pilot in Q2. Procurement and facilities need to approve rack space and power, and security needs the attestation. Do you typically do an on-site proof-of-concept?
[04:50] Ethan: Yes, typical POC is 4–6 weeks: initial discovery, on-prem install in a lab environment, run benchmark workloads, validate security controls, then expand. We can adapt to a lighter bench if you just want the runtime bench.
[05:01] Michael: Bench specifics — we'd like to run throughput and tail-latency tests with our tokenization and a few in-house prompts. Can Redwood run those or provide tooling?
[05:09] Priya: We provide a benchmark harness you can run locally; we can run an initial benchmark with you over a screenshare and then hand off scripts to run in your CI.
[05:18] Samir: Any OS or infra pre-reqs? We run RHEL7 in some places and Ubuntu 22.04 in others; some hosts are air-gapped so package managers are restricted.
[05:27] Priya: Our supported OS list is Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 and RHEL 8.x for the runtime. For air-gapped installs we provide an appliance bundle with OS packages included and SHA256 checksums for offline installation.
[05:38] Laura: How are secrets managed for integrations, like DB creds or SSO? We use an internal Vault.
[05:44] Priya: We support HashiCorp Vault and other secret backends; the operator config pulls secrets at runtime with short TTLs. For extremely restricted setups we can provide a static sealed secret approach with your KMS.
[05:55] Ethan: Quick question — who will be the primary stakeholders on your side for a pilot?
[05:59] Dr. Ana: It'll be Michael for ML, Samir for IT, Laura for security, and I will sponsor. Procurement will step in for contracts.
[06:08] Ethan: Perfect. About costs — for Dedicated/reserved vs private on-prem, the pricing model is different; for private on-prem there's a platform fee plus deployment support. We'll put together a rough TCO for your hardware and our support.
[06:21] Samir: On hardware, can you provide guidance for GPU counts for the 70B model with 1k RPS target? We can approximate but want Redwood's recommended cluster.
[06:31] Priya: We'll produce a capacity plan; rough ballpark for 70B at ~1k RPS depends on batching and latency SLO; might be multiple nodes with 8x80GB GPUs with NVLink per node, or sharded multi-node config. We'll run math and include cost estimates.
[06:46] Michael: One more — do you support model eval/quality monitoring hooks? We want drift detection and automated regression alerts.
[06:53] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring; for private installs we can ship the telemetry collector that pushes metrics to your observability stack or store locally. Alerts can be tied to prompt sets and evals.
[07:05] Laura: About legal — we need indemnities and data processing terms. We'll involve procurement.
[07:10] Ethan: Understood; we'll share standard EULA and data processing addendum; for enterprise installs we can negotiate terms.
[07:16] Priya: Ok, shifting to next steps — from an SE standpoint we'll provide an on-prem deployment checklist and a preflight script you can run.
[07:24] Michael: Great. Can we also get a sample of the offline installer and the checksum process so our infra team can review?
[07:30] Priya: Yes — we'll include the offline installer sample and the signature verification steps.
[07:35] Samir: Who will assist on the facilities side for rack/power questions during procurement?
[07:39] Ethan: I'll be the point for commercial and coordination; Priya will lead technical. We'll include our deployment engineer contact for on-site assistance.
[07:48] Dr. Ana: Sounds good. Any immediate blockers from Redwood?
[07:51] Ethan: None we can't work around — main dependencies are your facilities confirmation and security checklist completion.
[07:57] Laura: Ok. Let's talk dates: if we want a pilot in Q2, what's the earliest start?
[08:02] Priya: If facilities and procurement move in the next 2–3 weeks, we can schedule an on-site install and bench in early May. Otherwise we can do a remote lab install first.
[08:13] Dr. Ana: We'll push internally; procurement likes numbers.
[08:17] Ethan: Ok, wrap-up — we'll send the security pack, SOC2 report, offline installer sample, deployment checklist, and a preliminary TCO and capacity plan.
[08:26] Michael: Perfect. Thanks all.
[08:28] Dr. Ana: Thanks everyone.
[08:30] Ethan: Thanks, we'll follow up with materials and propose dates.
[08:33] [END]
